# Proverbs 17 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 17:2 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | A-servant [who]-acts-wisely will-rule over-a-son [who]-acts-shamefully, and-in-[the]-midst-of brothers he-will-share [the]-inheritance. |
| LOGOS | A servant who deals wisely will rule over a son who acts shamefully and will share the inheritance as one of the brothers. |
| PNEUMA | A wise servant will end up in charge of a disgraceful son and will share the inheritance right alongside the other children. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 17:4 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | An-evildoer gives-heed to-lips-of iniquity; falsehood listens to-a-tongue-of destruction. |
| LOGOS | An evildoer listens to wicked lips, and a liar gives ear to a mischievous tongue. |
| PNEUMA | Bad people love listening to destructive talk, and liars are drawn to a poisonous tongue. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

## 17:5 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | One-mocking [the]-poor reproaches his-Maker; one-rejoicing at-calamity will-not-go-unpunished. |
| LOGOS | Whoever mocks the poor insults his Maker; he who is glad at calamity will not go unpunished. |
| PNEUMA | Mocking someone because they're poor is an insult to the God who made them. Celebrating someone's misfortune will not go unpunished. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.

| EMET | Not fitting for-a-fool [are]-lips-of excellence; how-much-less for-a-noble [are]-lips-of falsehood. |
| LOGOS | Fine speech is not becoming to a fool; still less is false speech to a prince. |
| PNEUMA | Eloquent words don't fit a fool — and lies are even more disgraceful coming from a leader. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus. EMET preserves source-language structure; PNEUMA captures interpretive meaning. All three contribute valid perspectives.
